svg.title: Daily Cisco phone boot: current operation and proposed TFTP separation
svg.desc: The phone loads firmware from flash, requests configuration from TFTP and establishes fresh SIP registration. Current operation reopens a bounded restricted TFTP window before an authorized reboot. A proposed daily profile-only service has no firmware volume and must pass boot, firewall and exclusive port ownership gates before deployment. One IP allowlist is not per-device or per-file authentication.
svg.text: A stored firmware image is only part of boot
Configuration availability and fresh registration must be checked separately.
Verify both lines after this boot
Old contacts and web access are not proof
Reopen the reviewed restricted window before an authorized reboot
Exact accepted files → source-limited UDP → reboot → fresh registration → close and verify cleanup
Read-only file allowlist · no firmware volume · one TFTP port owner
First prove profile-only boot, guarded owner changes and firewall compatibility.
Never share the same listening ports.
Keep default DROP rules. The current external-SIP guard requires TFTP closed; migrate that contract first.
Source IP is not authentication. An allowed phone can request other profiles in a shared TFTP root.
